text:
Alice: Heads-up :warning: planning a staggered reboot window this Saturday 02:00-06:00 UTC for rack PSU firmware fallback tests in us-east1-rack-7. Expect ~15% shared capacity reduction during peak of the window. We want to do rolling reboots (one node per 10m) with canary verification and KV cache warmup before switching traffic back.

Ben: Quick q — will Dedicated pools be touched or only shared-hosted pools?

Alice: Only shared-hosted pools (standard/gpu-shared). Dedicated customers who pinned hardware are unaffected unless they've opted into shared maintenance. Canary nodes: `ue1-r7-n12`, `ue1-r7-n23`, `ue1-r7-n34`.

Dmitri: Cost and availability impact? Any plan to pause preemptible/spot assignments to avoid churn during reboots?

Eva: Recommend pausing spot churn and preheating burst capacity. I'm going to bump autoscaler min for the shared pool for the window. Patch will add a temporary buffer +30 nodes.

Alice: OpsBot, please create maintenance ticket + calendar invite for oncall and SRE ops.

OpsBot: Scheduled maintenance created: https://redwood.ops/maint/1767001111 — invites sent to #eng-infra-oncall, #eng-sre, and product-alerts. :white_check_mark:

Sam: We should seed KV prefix cache and run a small traffic canary against the three nodes before we cut main traffic. Suggest using the warmup script: ```./scripts/kv_warmup.sh --targets ue1-r7-n12,ue1-r7-n23,ue1-r7-n34 --duration 5m``` will populate prefix caches and reduce first-token latency spike.

Ben: I'll throttle noncritical batch jobs starting 01:30 UTC and drain queue workers on those racks. Command I'll run: ```for q in batch-*-workers; do ./ctl pause $q; done``` — will post ripple status.

Alice: Assigning ops: @Ben -> pause batch jobs, @Dmitri -> run canary health checks and report, @Eva -> confirm autoscaler bump + rollback plan, @Sam -> run KV warmup and confirm latencies.

Dmitri: Canary health checks executed at 02:05 UTC: all services responding, tail latency P95 = 42ms on canaries, GPU utilization steady. Paste of quick check: ```curl -sS http://ue1-r7-n12/health || true
{"status":"ok","p95_ms":"42"}``` — looks green.

Eva: Autoscaler patch applied, added hot-buffer of 30 nodes and set scale-down disabled during window. Patch diff (abridged): ```{"pool":"gpu-shared","autoscaler":{"min_replicas":"150","buffer":"30","scale_down":"disabled"}}``` Will revert at 06:15 UTC.

Ben: Batch pause done at 01:32 UTC. I'll start gradual resume after 06:30 UTC with a 20% ramp every 10m.

Alice: Note: expect egress spike while caches warm => rough cost estimate +$1.2k for the window (mainly S3 and cross-AZ). We can cap egress throttle if it looks bad.

Sam: I'll make a tiny dashboard to watch prefix hit-rate and first-token latency, and alert if P95 > 200ms or cache-hit < 60%.

Dmitri: If anything flaps we follow rollback playbook: take rack out of rotation, revert firmware, re-add. Postmortem if >15m outage. Agree?

Alice: Yes. Please annotate the maintenance ticket with rollback steps and cost notes. Thanks everyone — will post once we start the first canary. :thumbsup:

Ben: Thanks — will keep updates short and frequent in this thread.

Alice: Starting canary now 02:00 UTC.
